description: Issue #839: at RUN TIME a profile keyword is a built-in name unconditionally. `execute()` has no active profile set — it runs every profile's primitives and the reader recognises all six block heads regardless of profile — so the declaration-slot guard cannot be gated on one, and `spec/grammar.md`'s rule (maintainer ruling #833 rule 4) says it must not be: "a name that could be declared in one implementation but not in another would be invisible and unpredictable to a learner". So `define ask` halts at phase-1 registration with `ol-reserved-word` and the `ask` call on line 4 never runs. This fixture was added because a mutation removing profile keywords from the runtime's built-in-name lookup passed the ENTIRE conformance corpus: `sprites/reserved-procedures-with-sprites` and its `-without-sprites` pair are both `"check": true`, so nothing in the corpus executed one of these names. KNOWN RESIDUAL, deliberately documented rather than hidden: `check()` under Core alone still accepts `define ask` (`reserved-procedures-without-sprites` pins exactly that), so the two stages disagree for profile-gated names in the direction opposite to the one #839 closed. Retiring `checker-reserved-word.ts`'s profile gate is issue #841's always-on built-in-names list; when it lands, that fixture inverts and this one is unaffected.

diagnostics.message: ask is already part of OpenLogo. choose another name.
